title: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
description: Understand Azure RBAC, built-in roles, custom roles, and how scope controls access across subscriptions, resource groups, and individual resources.

data.text: **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)** is how Azure decides who can do what. Instead of sharing credentials, RBAC assigns an **identity** (user, group, or service principal) a **role** at a specific **scope**.

items: **Security principal** — The user, group, service principal, or managed identity receiving the role assignment.
**Role definition** — A set of permissions (like Reader, Contributor, or Owner). Azure provides built-in roles; you can also create custom ones.
**Scope** — The boundary where the role applies. Scope can be a management group, subscription, resource group, or a single resource.
**Role assignment** — The act of binding a principal + role + scope together. Access is granted by creating assignments; it is denied by default.

rows: Create and manage resources, but cannot grant access
Full access to Key Vault (keys, secrets, certificates)
Manage VMs but not the virtual network

data.title: Azure RBAC role assignment (ARM template)
data.content: A role assignment grants a user access to a resource group using the Contributor role.

data.title: Least Privilege
data.text: Always assign the lowest role that gets the job done. Contributor is safer than Owner, and Reader is safer still.

data.title: Practice: Assign Reader Access
data.description: Using the Azure portal, find the resource group named 'demo-rg'. Assign the Reader role to your own user account at that resource group scope. Verify you can see resources but cannot create new ones.
steps: Open the Azure portal and navigate to 'demo-rg'
Select Access control (IAM) from the left menu
Select the Reader role and click Next
Under Members, select your user account
data.expectedOutcome: The role assignment appears in the Access control list, and you can view all resources in the group without edit permissions.
